title: Agentic Kubernetes Assistant
description: A multi-agent diagnostic assistant that separates observation, remediation and human approval.
notes: TCS Xcelerate project using diagnostic, analysis, remediation, executor and safety-supervisor agents.
Read-only tools inspect pod status, logs and events. Restarts, image updates and scaling wait for human approval in Slack.
Local incident scenarios include ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled and liveness-probe failures.

title: Mini-Redis
description: A Redis-compatible key-value server built over raw TCP, with RESP parsing and expiry.
notes: Streaming RESP parser without a third-party protocol library.
Commands include PING, SET, GET, DEL, INCR and TTL, with passive and background expiration.
The added web interface uses the repository’s Python twin in-process; it does not control the separate Java server.

title: MiniDB
description: An embedded relational engine with its own page format, buffer pool and B+ tree.
notes: 4 KB slotted pages, free-space bitmap, LRU buffer pool and dirty-page tracking.
Persistent on-disk B+ tree with leaf splits and range scans.
SQL subset supports CREATE, INSERT, SELECT, DELETE, WHERE and ORDER BY.

title: LaptopHub
description: A React e-commerce application with filtering, a cart, wishlist and responsive layouts.
notes: The CV reports a 95+ Lighthouse performance score and approximately 40% improved product discoverability.
Cart and wishlist use Context API; layouts support phone, tablet and desktop, with dark mode.
No verified repository or live deployment link was supplied for this project.

title: Memory-backed ReAct Agent
description: Working, episodic and semantic memory that can update facts instead of accumulating stale preferences.
notes: Hashed embeddings and cosine similarity support memory retrieval.
Calculator and memory tools are integrated into a ReAct loop.
The repository runs offline with a heuristic MockLLM; this portfolio does not imply live model inference.

title: minic · C Compiler
description: A subset C compiler that turns source code into x86-64 System V assembly.
notes: Recursive-descent parsing, type handling, local stack offsets and code generation.
Supports integer expressions, pointers, functions, conditionals and loops.
The browser interface compiles submitted source to assembly only; it does not execute submitted programs.

title: Private Meta-search
description: Self-hosted search infrastructure with aggregation, rate limiting and cleaner result URLs.
notes: SearXNG stack with Redis rate limiting, reverse-proxy TLS and client-IP stripping.
Python aggregator runs engines in parallel, removes tracking parameters and re-ranks results.
Offline catalog and optional live Wikipedia mode are distinct from the SearXNG deployment.

title: Snapshot & Rollback Engine
description: A Linux storage engine with copy-on-write blocks, named snapshots and CRC-32 integrity checks.
notes: Immutable append-only block records and atomic metadata replacement.
Named snapshots, rollback, persistence and integrity verification.
An optional character driver is separate from the user-space engine.

title: CPU Scheduler & Deadlock Simulator
description: Operating-system simulations for scheduling and safe resource allocation.
notes: FCFS and Round Robin scheduling implementations described in the CV.
Banker’s Algorithm rejects unsafe allocations.
No verified repository or live deployment link was supplied.

title: Expense Tracker
description: A persistent Python/SQLite expense ledger with validation and spending reports.
notes: Add, view and delete expenses; money is stored as integer cents.
Monthly and category reports use SQL aggregation.
A separate local web frontend connects to the original database implementation.

title: Systems Engineering Lab
description: A collection of five implementations that expose the mechanics behind everyday abstractions.
notes: Includes a Redis server, database engine, memory-backed agent, private search and C compiler.
Each implementation remains independently usable.
The lab’s own frontend exposes all five tools within that repository.

title: E-commerce Website Collection
description: An existing collection of storefront, checkout, registration and contact pages.
notes: Static website pages are preserved in the repository.
These pages are distinct from the React LaptopHub project described in the CV.
Original checkout/registration pages are demos, not production payment or account systems.

title: Birthday Website
description: An interactive, personal birthday website with a dedicated local preview.

title: Birthday · Photo Edition
description: A photo-based edition of the birthday website.

title: Meta-search Workspace
description: A starter search interface added to the previously empty meta-search repository.
notes: Uses the aggregator from the separate private-metasearch-engine repository.
Offline catalog with optional live Wikipedia lookup.

title: Copilot · School Activities
description: A learning repository with a school activities app and a persistent registration adapter.

title: OctoFit Tracker
description: A local fitness-tracking prototype alongside the Copilot course’s unfinished application skeleton.
notes: Working local workout log and leaderboard.
The added prototype is not completion of the course’s Django/MongoDB stack.

title: Stack Overflown
description: A developer-themed browser puzzle game in the Git introduction exercise repository.
